subject: Re: GCP private offer — depletion trigger & accelerated drawdown playbook
messages:
From: Sara Lin <sara.lin@orionai.com>
To: Mina Haddad <mina@redwood.com>
Cc: Evan Park <evan.park@nimbuscloud.io>
Date: Mon, 18 May 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: GCP private offer — depletion trigger & accelerated drawdown

Hi Mina,

Quick note from procurement — Orion's usage on the new test clusters has spiked unexpectedly and we're bumping against the committed spend cadence for our GCP private offer. We have the PO attached (Orion_PO_0526.pdf).

We need to understand options for:
- triggering depletion credits earlier (mid-quarter) if commit thresholds are met
- an accelerated drawdown schedule so we don’t carry a large unused balance into next quarter
- billing alignment (invoice dates and any rebate mechanics)

Can Redwood provide a short playbook or steps we can put into our procurement checklist? A one-page matrix showing trigger thresholds, accounting treatment, and expected invoice flow would be super helpful. Also please confirm whether any approvals are required on Redwood's side to frontload drawdown or apply an early depletion event.

If useful, Evan from Nimbus (copied) has handled similar private offers on other marketplaces and can join a short call.

Appreciate a quick turnaround — procurement needs guidance by Friday.

Thanks,
Sara
Sara Lin
Head of Procurement, Orion AI
procurement@orionai.com

Date: Mon, 18 May 2026 11:05:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: GCP private offer — depletion trigger & accelerated drawdown

Sara — thanks for the clear ask and for attaching the PO. We'll put together a concise playbook and confirm approval paths.

Immediate notes:
- We can support an accelerated drawdown schedule for customers who accelerate consumption; it typically requires: confirmation of the PO, finance alignment on invoice timing, and a short change-order (internal approval) to reflect the drawdown dates.
- Depletion triggers are configurable per-offer. We have two common approaches: automatic depletion on a rolling 30/60 day burn check, or a manual depletion action triggered by customer request + approval.

Marissa — can you confirm whether Revenue needs a signed amendment for mid-quarter drawdown and if there are any rebate mechanics that must be recorded?
Jonas — can you confirm GCP marketplace constraints (DocuSign or billing-side window) and whether we need a private-offer amendment with Google?
Ben — please prepare the redwood-drawdown-calculator.xlsx with example numbers (we can use Orion's usage from the PO) so we can show the cashflow impact and invoice dates.

Sara — we'll aim to send the one-page matrix and a proposed change-order template by EOD Thursday and schedule a 30-minute sync if that helps.

Best,
Mina Haddad
Head of Sales, North America
Redwood Inference
mina@redwood.com

From: Jonas Weber <jonas@redwood.com>
To: Mina Haddad <mina@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 19 May 2026 08:43:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: GCP private offer — depletion trigger & accelerated drawdown

Heads up and a suggested play:

On Tue, May 18, 2026 at 11:05 AM Mina Haddad <mina@redwood.com> wrote:
> Sara — thanks for the clear ask and for attaching the PO. We'll put together a concise playbook and confirm approval paths.

Quick answers from GCP/partner side:
- Google permits private-offer amendments to adjust redemption windows; typically the merchant submits an amendment request and Google processes it within ~3 business days.
- For early depletion triggers we should avoid automated mid-quarter depletion unless the customer explicitly agrees; that avoids surprises on both sides. Manual-trigger approach + signed change-order is lowest friction.
- We can frontload drawdown (apply more committed units earlier) but we need a clear invoice mapping so bookkeeping matches the customer's ledger and Google’s marketplace ledger.

Attached a simple calculator (redwood-drawdown-calculator.xlsx) with three scenarios:
A) Manual mid-quarter depletion (customer requests depletion event; invoice shift applies same month)
B) Accelerated scheduled drawdown (customer elects larger monthly consumption credit over next 2 months)
C) Rebate/true-up at quarter end (least operational lift but slower cash flow alignment)

Recommended playbook (short):
1) Customer requests depletion/acceleration (email + PO copy)
2) Sales/Finance prepare amendment and calculator output, share with customer
3) Customer signs amendment (DocuSign link)
4) We file amendment with Google if it affects marketplace redemption window
5) Finance issues updated invoice schedule and confirms tax/billing treatment

Jonas
Head of Partnerships, Redwood Inference
jonas@redwood.com

Attachment: redwood-drawdown-calculator.xlsx (application/vnd.openxmlformats-officedocument.spreadsheetml.sheet, 14 KB)
From: Mina Haddad <mina@redwood.com>
To: Sara Lin <sara.lin@orionai.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>, Jonas Weber <jonas@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 21 May 2026 16:03:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: GCP private offer — depletion trigger & accelerated drawdown

Sara — following up with the deliverables we discussed. Below is the short playbook and next steps. I included links to the HubSpot deal and a draft amendment (DocuSign link) for your review.

Short playbook (one-pager summary):
- Trigger options: manual depletion (customer-triggered) | scheduled acceleration (customer elects frontload) | quarter-end true-up (no mid-quarter invoice changes)
- Approval: internal Finance + Revenue sign-off required for any frontloading that changes invoice amounts prior to existing invoice cadence
- GCP steps: if the amendment changes the redemption window, Redwood files the amendment with Google; otherwise amendment stays between Redwood and customer and we map invoice schedule to the existing private offer SKU redemption.
- Timeline: typical turnaround is 2–5 business days after receipt of signed amendment (3 days for Google processing when filing with Marketplace).

Proposed next steps:
1) Review the attached calculator scenario B (accelerated scheduled drawdown) and confirm which months to apply the frontload.
2) If Orion approves, sign the draft amendment here: https://www.docusign.com/parties/ORION-GCP-PO
3) We will then file with Google (if required) and issue an updated invoice schedule.

Links: HubSpot deal — https://app.hubspot.com/deals/1234567; Draft amendment/DocuSign — https://www.docusign.com/parties/ORION-GCP-PO; Playbook PDF (drive) — https://drive.google.com/file/d/1RedwoodPlaybook/view

Marissa — please confirm Revenue's note on whether we need a formal credit memo or if we can treat the frontloaded units as prepaid applied across invoices.
Ben — please create the invoice schedule draft after Sara confirms months.

Sara — happy to hop on a 30-minute call Monday to finalize.

Thanks,
Mina Haddad
Head of Sales, North America
Redwood Inference
mina@redwood.com

On a related note, Evan (Nimbus) — if you have a template amendment that worked previously for your customers, please paste it into the HubSpot deal file so we can reuse language.
